marks.gloss_en: Rav Huna (9a): an animal in its lifetime stands in a presumption of prohibition until you know how it was slaughtered
אף אנן נמי תנינא: R' Shimon, 'if he paused the length of an examination' -- מאי לאו כדי ביקור סימנין? so examining the simanim is required
the slaughterer must examine the simanim after slaughter
לא, הכי אמר רבי יוחנן: כדי ביקור חכם -- the mishna's examination is of the knife by a sage, not of the simanim
אם כן נתת דבריך לשיעורין! -- then the measure varies with circumstance (how near the sage is). Unattributed; Steinsaltz gives it to Rav Yosef
אלא כדי ביקור טבח חכם -- rather, the length of an examination by a sage-slaughterer (= p_bikur_tabach_chacham)
R' Yochanan: [R' Shimon's measure is] the length of an examination by a sage
במאי קמיפלגי? בדרב הונא -- the nevela-holder extends Rav Huna's presumption of prohibition past death
במאי קמיפלגי? בדרב הונא -- the tereifa-holder applies the presumption to prohibition only, not to impurity
an animal in its life stands in a presumption of prohibition until you know how it was slaughtered
כדבעא מיניה רבי אבא מרב הונא -- Rav Huna's own ruling on the returned perforated innards shows the presumption survives a flaw
איידי דממשמשא ידא דטבחא מפתת -- since the slaughterer's hand handles it, it crumbles
איתיביה: a bird pecking a fig, a mouse gnawing melons -- we DO suspect it pecked at a perforation
a Torah scholar must learn writing
any slaughterer who does not know the halakhot of slaughter -- one may not eat from his slaughter
the dictum is needed for one who slaughtered well before us two or three times: since he did not learn, sometimes he pauses or presses and does not know it
[if he did not examine the simanim:] it is tereifa and forbidden to eat
it stands in its presumption of prohibition, and now it is dead [so it is nevela]
[innards a wolf took and returned perforated:] we do not suspect that it perforated at the place of a perforation
